lead: Detroit plumbing deals with deep cold, old brick homes, lead lines and basement flooding. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Detroit.
risk: lead service lines, basement flooding and frozen pipes
risk_short: lead lines, basement flooding and frozen pipes
why: Most Detroit homes were built before 1950. Boston-Edison, Indian Village and Grandmont-Rosedale have grand older homes with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead service lines. The city is replacing lead lines over time.
Heavy storms, like the summer 2021 floods, overload the combined sewers and flood basements. Winter cold freezes pipes, especially in vacant or partly heated homes.
water: Detroit's water is treated by the Great Lakes Water Authority from the Detroit River and Lake Huron. It is moderately soft. DWSD runs a lead service line replacement program.
tips: Check DWSD's lead line program for your street.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Keep the heat on in winter, even in empty homes.
areas: PipeMend works in Midtown, Corktown, Indian Village, Boston-Edison, Palmer Woods, Grandmont-Rosedale, Southwest Detroit and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the city's Buildings, Safety Engineering and Environmental Department (BSEED), and plumbers must be licensed by Michigan LARA.

faq.a: Most of Detroit has combined sewers that carry rain and wastewater together. Big storms fill them, and water backs up through floor drains. A backwater valve and a sump pump help protect the basement.
